subject: Science
title: Sand and soil
objectives: Children will play with sand and soil using hands and tools.
Children will notice that wet sand and dry sand feel different.
content: Playing with sand and soil, digging, and noticing that wet and dry sand feel different.
teachingActivities: Let children dig and scoop freely; name each action; use small tools; keep sand away from eyes; model washing hands after play.
learnerActivities: Dig and scoop sand and soil with tools and say wet or dry for sand.
resources: Spoons, scoops, small buckets and trowels
assessment: Observe whether each child digs or scoops with a tool and says wet or dry for sand.
expectedOutcomes: Digs or scoops sand or soil with a tool.
Says wet or dry for sand.

lessons.title: Playing with sand
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will play with dry sand using hands and tools.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with water and say wet and dry, float and sink.
lessons.starter: Let sand run through your fingers and say "Sand. It is soft and it falls."
teacherActivities: Show how to scoop sand into a bucket and pour it out.
Let children feel the sand with their hands.
Fill a small bucket and turn it upside down to make a sand shape.
learnerActivities: Children scoop and pour.
Child touches the sand and says sand.
Child makes a shape in the sand.
Child says pour, fall or scoop.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to scoop sand into a bucket and pour it out. Children: Children scoop and pour.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children feel the sand with their hands. Children: Child touches the sand and says sand.
Step 3. Teacher: Fill a small bucket and turn it upside down to make a sand shape. Children: Child makes a shape in the sand.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What can sand do?" Children: Child says pour, fall or scoop.

practical.title: Sand tray
steps: Set up a sand tray on a mat.
Scoop and pour sand with tools.
practical.safety: Keep sand away from eyes and mouths. Use clean sand and wash hands afterwards. Sweep up spilled sand to avoid slipping.

differentiation.support: Scoop together with a hand over the child’s hand.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to fill two buckets and say which has more.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What can you do with sand?

lessons.conclusion: Tidy the sand and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child play in sand at the compound or park.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "play with dry sand using hands and tools" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Digging in soil
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will dig in soil and look for small creatures with a spoon.
successCriteria: Digs in soil with a tool
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with water and say wet and dry, float and sink.
lessons.starter: Hold a handful of soil and say "This is soil. Plants grow in soil." Let it fall.
teacherActivities: Show how to dig with a spoon and put soil in a bucket.
Let children touch the soil and describe it.
Look for small stones or roots in the soil with a magnifying glass.
learnerActivities: Children dig and fill the bucket.
Child touches the soil and says soft or dark.
Child looks and points.
Children wash hands with soap.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to dig with a spoon and put soil in a bucket. Children: Children dig and fill the bucket.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children touch the soil and describe it. Children: Child touches the soil and says soft or dark.
Step 3. Teacher: Look for small stones or roots in the soil with a magnifying glass. Children: Child looks and points.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Wash hands" after digging. Children: Children wash hands with soap.

practical.title: Digging soil
steps: Set up a tray of clean soil.
Look at what is in the soil.
practical.safety: Use clean potting soil and wash hands after every session. Do not allow children to put soil in their mouths and cover any cuts.

differentiation.support: Dig together and name the tool.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find three different things in the soil.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Digs in soil with a tool
lessons.conclusion: Wash hands and say "Thank you, soil."
lessons.homeConnection: Dig in the garden with your child and wash hands afterwards.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "dig in soil and look for small creatures with a spoon" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Wet sand and dry sand
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will feel the difference between wet and dry sand.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with water and say wet and dry, float and sink.
resources: Two trays: dry sand and wet sand
lessons.starter: Pour dry sand through your fingers, then wet sand. Say "Dry sand falls. Wet sand sticks."
teacherActivities: Pour dry sand and let it run through your fingers.
Pour a little water on sand and mix.
Try to make a sandcastle with dry sand and then wet sand.
learnerActivities: Children feel the dry sand.
Children watch and feel the wet sand.
Child tries both and sees which works.
Child points to the wet sand.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pour dry sand and let it run through your fingers. Children: Children feel the dry sand.
Step 2. Teacher: Pour a little water on sand and mix. Children: Children watch and feel the wet sand.
Step 3. Teacher: Try to make a sandcastle with dry sand and then wet sand. Children: Child tries both and sees which works.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "Which sand makes a shape?" Children: Child points to the wet sand.

practical.title: Sandcastles
steps: Turn them over to make castles.
Try with dry sand and compare.
practical.safety: Keep sand away from eyes and wash hands afterwards. Use shallow water and wipe spills.

differentiation.support: Feel both sands together and say the words.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to wet and mix a tray of sand.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is this sand wet or dry?

expectedOutcomes: Says wet or dry for sand
Makes a shape with wet sand
lessons.conclusion: Tidy the sand trays and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Make a sandcastle with wet sand at home or at the park.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "feel the difference between wet and dry sand" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sand and soil play
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will explore sand and soil together in play.
successCriteria: Uses sand and soil in play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with water and say wet and dry, float and sink.
lessons.starter: Show plastic animals and say "Let us make a farm in the sand."
teacherActivities: Show how to make a road in the sand with a finger.
Show how to make a garden with soil.
Put animals on the farm and ask "What are you making?"
Ask "How is sand different from soil?"
learnerActivities: Children make roads.
Children dig a small garden.
Child tells you what they are making.
Child says a word such as dark or light.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to make a road in the sand with a finger. Children: Children make roads.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how to make a garden with soil. Children: Children dig a small garden.
Step 3. Teacher: Put animals on the farm and ask "What are you making?" Children: Child tells you what they are making.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How is sand different from soil?" Children: Child says a word such as dark or light.

practical.title: Sand farm
steps: Set up trays of sand and soil.
Make roads, gardens and a farm.
Tell a friend what you made.
practical.safety: Keep sand and soil away from faces and wash hands afterwards. Supervise sharing.

differentiation.support: Play beside the child and name what they make.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to make a long road and a small garden.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Plays creatively with sand and soil
lessons.conclusion: Tidy the trays and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Play with sand or soil outdoors and talk about what you make.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "explore sand and soil together in play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 8 sand and soil check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child plays with sand and soil.
successCriteria: Digs or scoops with a tool
Says wet or dry for sand
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can play with water and say wet and dry, float and sink.
lessons.starter: Sing "Scoop, scoop, scoop the sand" and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: dry sand, wet sand and soil.
At each station ask "What are you doing?" and "Is it wet or dry?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or action.
Children wash hands and tidy.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: dry sand, wet sand and soil. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What are you doing?" and "Is it wet or dry?" Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children wash hands and tidy.

practical.title: Sand and soil stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station closely. Keep sand away from eyes and wash hands after each station.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to explain what they made.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: digs or scoops; says wet or dry for sand; says soil and sand.

questions.question: Is the sand wet or dry?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
Plays safely with sand and soil
lessons.homeConnection: Play with sand or soil at home and wash hands afterwards.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child plays with sand and soil" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
